name: veterinary_clinic_system_056_lab_flag_summary
instruction: Produce the lab flag snapshot for this episode under the batch code in ops_meta. The snapshot has three parts, all derived from live lab_results and the patients join. (1) Rollup: one ops_reports row report='lab_flag_summary' with critical, abnormal, normal, total counts over all lab_results, plus pct_critical, pct_abnormal, and pct_flagged rounded to one decimal. (2) By-test breakdown: one ops_reports row report='lab_flag_by_test' per distinct test_name, each with test_name, critical, abnormal, normal, and total for that test. (3) By-species breakdown: one ops_reports row report='lab_flag_by_species' per species present among the patients referenced by lab_results (join patients), each with species, critical, abnormal, normal, total, and pct_of_total (round(100*species_total/rollup_total,1)). Any lab result whose patient_id cannot be resolved to a patient is counted under species='unknown'. If any of these report rows already exist for this batch, delete and rewrite them so the report is current. Do not modify lab_results or patients.
_max_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.
_par_steps_note: Measure via live gold run in QC session; do not guess.

success_criteria.summary: From seed: 42 lab_results with flag counts critical=1, abnormal=10, normal=31. Rollup row must match these counts plus pct_critical=2.4, pct_abnormal=23.8, pct_flagged=26.2. By-test rows: CBC(3abn,4norm,7total), FeLV/FIV snap test(3norm), Fecal ova & parasites(1abn,5norm), Heartworm antigen(2abn,2norm), SDMA(1abn), Serum chemistry panel(1crit,7norm), Thyroid panel (T4)(5norm), Urinalysis(3abn,5norm). By-species rows: canine(1crit,7abn,15norm,23total,54.8%), equine(1norm), exotic(1norm), feline(3abn,14norm,17total,40.5%). All rows must carry the batch_code and be the only rows of those report types for this batch. Dual-path counts (Python vs SQL) must agree.

checks.expect: exactly 13 rows (1 rollup + 8 by-test + 4 by-species) keyed by report type and batch_code
every count in rollup, by-test, and by-species recomputed via SQL and Python; both agree

hazards: lab_results id=1 is the only 'critical' row (Serum chemistry panel, patient 4). A solution that folds 'critical' into 'abnormal' will report critical=0 and abnormal=11 and fail the rollup.

lab_results id=7 references patient 27, whose patients row has status='transferred' (row evidence: patient id=27 species='feline' status='transferred'). A solution that excludes transferred-patient labs from the snapshot will under-count feline to 16 and total to 41; 056 is a full snapshot and must include it.
The by-species breakdown requires a join through patients; a solution that counts raw lab rows without resolving patient species will miss the species grouping entirely.
The by-test and by-species row set is dynamic (test names and species appear only when present); a hardcoded row list will fail on reseed.
ops_reports must be delete-then-rewritten per batch to stay idempotent; duplicate or stale-batch rows fail the count checks.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Hardmode v2 turns a single count row into a three-level lab quality snapshot (rollup, by-test, by-species) with percentage fields and dual-path verification. It requires a patients join and treats 'critical' as its own category, not an abnormal variant.
